column2: Jot down product ideas, ways to improve work or creative directions. Add detail later.\n\nFor example: collect this week's challenges before the team meeting, then discuss solutions together.
Keep addresses, lists and meeting notes handy to read, copy and paste.\n\nFor example: pick up the repaired computer on Saturday at 2 pm. Bring the repair slip and power adapter.

Save a favorite line with its source and your thoughts, ready for writing or sharing.

For example: “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.” — Laozi
My thought: break a big goal into one small step I can take today.

Draft messages, emails or social posts here. Refine them before copying them out.\n\nFor example: Hi everyone, Friday's project meeting is now at 3 pm. Please prepare any questions and reply to confirm. Thanks!
Summarize methods and key facts in your own words for later review.\n\nFor example: after reading an article, note its main idea, add a practical example and list any questions you still have.

Discard old drafts, temporary notes or ideas you've set aside.

Select “Discard” to move a note to the bin. Click a paper ball to read it, then “Restore” to edit it in Notes again.

Use “Empty bin” to clear what you no longer need. Once confirmed, this cannot be undone.
Last week's pickup reminder is no longer needed, so it goes in the bin.\n\nTemporary information needn't stay in Notes. You can still open it to check before clearing it for good.
An event title idea: A Weekend Walk Together.\n\nThis version wasn't used, so it goes in the bin for now. Restore it later if you want to refer to it or try again.

Archive notes worth keeping, such as developed ideas, project reviews, study summaries and reusable drafts.

Archived notes move out of your daily workspace into Archive, where you can find and reuse them. This leaves Notes focused on work in progress.

Your archived content stays safe. Restore it whenever you want to edit it again.
